title: cloudflare credentials: CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID vs CF_ACCOUNT_ID mismatch + no global fallback in cloudflare.mk
description: mx infra setup cloudflare writes CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID to the global file (crates/mx-cli/src/commands/infra.rs:107-136) but the whole deploy toolchain reads CF_ACCOUNT_ID from the project file (templates/make/cloudflare.mk:16, cf-init-app.sh:121-123), so mx infra-managed credentials are never consumed. Also cloudflare.mk -includes only the project env file with no global fallback (line 15). Unify the var names and add resolution. Source: docs/development/mx-cloudflare-deploy.md section 6 items 2+4.

title: fix mx upgrade: reads non-existent templates/project/
description: mx upgrade fails against the current template layout: discover_upgrades reads <templates>/project (crates/mx-lib/src/upgrade/mod.rs:141-148) which does not exist, so every upgrade errors out. Either restructure templates/ to match or repoint discovery at the real layout. Blocks the migration flow in docs/development/mx-app-playbook.md section 4. Source: mx-app-playbook + mx-recipes-and-build gap inventories.

title: corpus ops hardening: Neon pooler statement cache, HNSW-vs-exact decision, ingest pipeline resilience
description: Research (pgvector-rust-batch-embedding.md, PR #20) found live risks: (1) we connect via Neon's -pooler endpoint with sqlx default statement cache → intermittent 'prepared statement already exists' class; set statement-cache-capacity=0. (2) category/language-filtered searches ride HNSW with default ef_search → pre-0.8-iterative-scan recall trap; at ~2k chunks exact search (drop/skip index) is the honest fix, revisit past 50k. (3) verify pgvector >=0.8.2 (CVE-2026-3172). (4) ingest hardening per the doc's Synthesis: token-aware batching (300k/request cap), backon retries + idempotent writes, buffer_unordered + bounded-channel writer when growth warrants.
acceptance_criteria: statement-cache-capacity=0 on pooled connections; filtered-search recall verified correct (exact search or iterative scans); pgvector version checked >=0.8.2; ingest survives injected 429/5xx with retries and never double-writes

title: corpus retrieval quality: inert pg_trgm lexical arm, RRF, eval harness
description: Research (rag-retrieval-fusion-and-chunking.md, PR #19) empirically verified our 0.15-weighted pg_trgm similarity() arm contributes ~0.003 of score separation vs the vector arm's ~0.2 — rag search is effectively vector-only. Fix ladder: strict_word_similarity (one-liner) → ts_rank_cd tsvector arm → real BM25; then retune weights or adopt the Katz RRF pattern (over-fetch 40/arm, UNION ALL, rrf_score). Prereq: 50-100 golden-query eval harness (nDCG@10 + recall@5 + token-IoU) so changes are measured, per the doc's Synthesis priority list.
acceptance_criteria: Eval harness exists with baseline numbers recorded; lexical arm demonstrates clean relevant-vs-irrelevant separation on the harness; fusion method (RRF or retuned CC) chosen by measured nDCG@10; corpus doc updated with the measured outcome

title: mx infra link/unlink are stubs with two incompatible link mechanisms
description: mx infra link/unlink only print a message (crates/mx-cli/src/commands/infra.rs:307-333). The Rust resolver expects a .env.linked marker file (crates/mx-lib/src/infra/config.rs:117) while the bash scripts and INFRA_CONFIG.md expect MX_INFRA_USE_GLOBAL=true inside the env file (cf-init-app.sh:102). Implement link/unlink for real and pick ONE mechanism. Source: mx-cloudflare-deploy.md section 6 item 3.

title: phantom mx cf command: implement or fix the docs
description: INFRA_CONFIG.md (mx cf setup/config/deploy) and the MCP server resource text (crates/mx-mcp-server/src/mcp/server.rs:357-359) document an mx cf subcommand that does not exist in the CLI (no Cf variant in main.rs Commands). Either implement mx cf as a wrapper over the make cf-* targets or purge/replace the doc references. Source: mx-cloudflare-deploy.md section 6 item 1.

title: unyform clients disagree on org path segment (id vs slug)
description: The CLI Unyform client sends the org id in /v1/orgs/{org}/... (crates/mx-lib/src/unyform/mod.rs:206-211) while the MCP client sends the org slug (crates/mx-mcp-server/src/unyform/mod.rs:258-267). One of them is wrong against api.unyform.ai; unify on a single client or at least a single convention. Source: mx-recipes-and-build gap inventory item 4.

title: recipe provenance lock + mx recipe diff (consumer update path)
description: Projects have zero record of which recipe+version generated their services (no lockfile; InstallResult discarded, installer.rs:401-409), so upstream recipe changes cannot be detected or propagated. Implement the native fix proposed in docs/development/mx-recipes-and-build.md section 4: mx add writes a docker/.config/recipe-lock.json entry, and a new mx recipe diff <svc> renders the current recipe to a temp dir and shows the delta.

title: Activate cross-model research provider (OpenAI consultation)
description: Flip the 'cross-model' entry in skills/technique-research/references/source-providers.md from planned to active: define query mechanics (OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint, model + base_url + key from env — OPENAI_API_KEY already in .env.secrets), response contract (claims cited as 'model consultation: <model>', confidence medium, corroborate-or-mark-inferred rule), and when-to-use (contested/judgment-heavy topics). Lets technique-research Phase 2 consult GPT alongside Claude orchestration. Mirrors GitHub issue Dev916/mech-crate#7.
acceptance_criteria: source-providers.md cross-model entry is Status: active with concrete Query/Returns/Cost mechanics; repo + home skill snapshots identical; a directed research run on a contested topic shows a 'model consultation' citation or an explicit skip rationale in the PR body

title: CF cron worker ships TODO KV namespace id; deploy fails until created
description: cf-init type=cron generates wrangler.toml with kv_namespaces id TODO_CREATE_KV_NAMESPACE — deploy fails until the user creates the namespace and pastes the id. Automate wrangler kv namespace create during cf-init or fail with clear instructions. Source: mx-cloudflare-deploy.md section 6 item 8.

title: mark appendix-build-deploy-recipe.md aspirational sections (layout drift)
description: The appendix prescribes infra/dockerfiles/ + containers-worker/ layout and a different cloudflare.mk than what mx actually scaffolds (docker/dockerfiles/<app>/app + infra/cloudflare/apps/<app>/). Annotate the drifted sections as aspirational/legacy and point at mx-cloudflare-deploy.md as ground truth. Source: mx-cloudflare-deploy.md section 6 item 6.

title: terraform: scaffold it or remove the promises
description: The generated .gitignore ignores tfstate/tfvars (new.rs:270-274) and appendix-build-deploy-recipe.md documents make terraform-* targets, but no *.tf exists anywhere in templates/ and no terraform targets exist. Either add a terraform template family or strip the references. Source: mx-cloudflare-deploy.md section 6 item 5.

title: mx doctor: add router checks
description: mx doctor validates structure/docker/make but performs zero router checks (crates/mx-cli/src/commands/doctor.rs; bin/lib/doctor.sh) — no devmesh-traefik network check, no mx-router container check, no port-80 ownership check. Add a router section so doctor catches the most common URL failures. Source: mx-app-playbook research.

title: mx router inspect parity + reload in the Rust CLI
description: Rust mx router inspect is a bare alias of status (crates/mx-cli/src/commands/router.rs:175-177) with no connected-services listing, and reload (SIGHUP hot-reload) exists only in bin/lib/router.sh:178-182. Port the shell inspect (docker network inspect devmesh-traefik enumeration) and reload into the Rust CLI. Source: mx-app-playbook research.

title: retire or router-wire the legacy port-publishing compose templates
description: templates/docker/compose/{app,app.dev,worker,nginx,traefik}.yml publish host ports, join mech-network, and carry no Traefik labels — the exact anti-pattern the router rule forbids, and a live port-80 conflict risk with mx-router (nginx/traefik samples bind 80/443). Either delete them or convert to router-wired reference samples. Source: mx-app-playbook research; mx-cloudflare-deploy port-conflict ladder.

title: wire testbed scaffold smoke tests into CI + add recipe.json validator
description: tests/testbed/*.test.sh scaffold smoke tests exist but are not run by any workflow (.github/workflows/release.yml is the only CI), and nothing validates the real on-disk recipe.json files (serde parse only; unknown fields like astro's npm_install and 'kebab' transform are silently ignored). Add a CI job + a strict recipe validator/linter. Source: mx-recipes-and-build gap inventory item 10.

title: recipe versioning discipline: dead version field, no changelog
description: Local recipe.json version fields are parsed but never read, displayed, compared, or gated (crates/mx-lib/src/recipe/parser.rs:26-28) and there is no changelog convention for recipe changes. Decide: surface versions in mx recipes list/info + bump discipline, or drop the field. Pairs with the recipe-lock issue. Source: mx-recipes-and-build gap inventory item 1.

title: source-root vs source marker file mismatch (mx init vs mx self-update)
description: mx init records the repo root at ~/.mech-crate/config/source-root (crates/mx-lib/src/paths.rs:17-21) but mx self-update's fallback reads ~/.mech-crate/source (crates/mx-cli/src/commands/self_update.rs:315) — that fallback can never find init's recording. Align on one path. Source: mx-recipes-and-build gap inventory item 9.

title: recipe apps missing release scripts: make release fails on fresh apps
description: make release app=<app> delegates to yarn release* scripts that recipe-generated apps do not ship (templates/recipes/nuxt/app/package.json has no release scripts or standard-version dep), so the conventional release path fails until bootstrapped by hand; only release-simple works. Ship the scripts in recipes or make release fall back gracefully. Source: mx-recipes-and-build gap inventory item 8.

title: mx build --platform silently dropped by the make layer
description:
mx build forwards platform=

as a make var (crates/mx-cli/src/commands/build.rs:93-102) but the _build target only passes $(nocache) as build.sh's 5th positional arg — platform never reaches docker. Wire it through like build-multiplatform does (extra args). Source: mx-recipes-and-build gap inventory item 6.

title: no make rebuild; compose never passes --build
description: rebuild is declared .PHONY in templates/make/common.mk:4 but never defined, and dev.sh/up.sh never pass --build, so stale images silently persist until a manual make build. Add a real rebuild target (and/or a dev flag) that forces image rebuild. Source: mx-recipes-and-build gap inventory item 7.

title: mx recipes apply --fix is a dead flag; advertised drift comparison unimplemented
description: apply's --fix parameter is bound as _fix and ignored (crates/mx-cli/src/commands/recipes.rs:206; tools/mod.rs:2358), and the MCP tool description promises dependency-drift and infrastructure comparison that is not implemented (recipe.dependencies/infrastructure parsed but never used). Implement or remove flag+claims. Source: mx-recipes-and-build gap inventory item 3.

title: CF generated Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK hits /health the app may not serve
description: cf-init's generated Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK curls http://localhost:PORT/health (cf-init-app.sh:900) but the worker's control routes are /_health etc — the container check only passes if the app itself serves /health, which nothing enforces or documents. Align the convention (require /health in onboarding docs) or generate a configurable path. Source: mx-cloudflare-deploy.md section 6 item 7.
